title: Frequency Reference
subtitle: A built-in, editable table of common APRS and EmComm frequencies for quick lookup in the field.
in_this_chapter: What the frequency reference is for
Opening it from the Map menu
Reading the list and the detail panel
Copy to clipboard and Reset to defaults

blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The **Frequency Reference** is a small, always-handy lookup table of the frequencies you actually use when you operate: APRS channels for different parts of the world, plus common EmComm calling frequencies, traffic nets, and the NOAA weather channels. It is a cheat sheet, not a radio control. APRS Command does not tune your rig from this window and it never transmits — the reference just shows you numbers you can read off, copy, and program into your radio by hand.

It ships pre-loaded so it is useful the moment you install the app. You can also make it your own: add your club's repeater, your local ARES net, or a park frequency, and those entries are saved and waiting the next time you open the window.

callout.label: Receive-first, always
callout.text: Like the rest of APRS Command, nothing here touches the air. The title bar keeps its **TX Disabled** badge whether or not this window is open. The reference only displays frequencies — dialing one in on your radio is a manual step you take yourself.

steps: A floating window titled **Frequency Reference** opens, centered over the main window.

blocks.p: The window is resizable and floats on top of the map, so you can keep it open beside the map page while you work. Close it any time — your entries are already saved.

blocks.screenshot: The Frequency Reference window: a scrolling list of frequencies on the left with column headers MHz, Mode, Name, Notes; a detail and action panel on the right showing the selected frequency in large type with Add, Edit, Delete, Copy, and Reset buttons.

blocks.p: Every new installation starts with a standard set of APRS and EmComm frequencies. You do not have to type these in — they are there from the first launch. The built-in entries cover:

bullets: **APRS voice/packet channels** — `144.390` for North America, `144.800` for Europe, `145.175` for Australia and New Zealand, `144.640` for Japan, and the North American alternate `144.340`, all __FM / 1200 baud__.
**HF APRS** — `10.151` on 30 meters and `14.105` on 20 meters, both __USB / 300 baud__.
**EmComm simplex calling** — the national VHF calling frequency `146.520` (2m) and UHF `446.000` (70cm), both __FM Simplex__.
**HF nets** — SHARES primary `5.1965`, and the National Traffic System nets `7.228` (40m) and `3.995` (80m).
**NOAA Weather Radio** — the seven WX channels from `162.400` through `162.550`, marked __NFM Receive__ (listen-only).

callout.label: Numbers are in MHz
callout.text: Every frequency in the list is shown in megahertz, so `144.390` means 144.390 MHz. The large number in the detail panel spells out ` MHz` after it so there is no guessing.

blocks.p: The list is laid out in four columns, with a header row along the bottom of the list so you always know which is which:

rows: How to operate it — for example `FM / 1200 baud`, `USB`, or `NFM Receive`.
A one-line description; trimmed with an ellipsis if it is long.

blocks.p: Click any row to select it. The panel on the right then shows that entry in full: the name, the frequency in large blue type followed by ` MHz`, the mode, and the complete notes text. If nothing is selected yet, the panel simply reads __Select a frequency to see details.__
The right-hand panel has five buttons for managing entries. To add your own frequency:

steps: Click **Add frequency**. The panel switches to an edit form and the status line reads "Enter details for the new frequency."
Fill in **Name *** (required) — for example `Club Net Repeater`.
Optionally set **Mode** (it starts at `FM Simplex`) and add a **Notes** description.
Click **Save**. Your entry is added, selected, and saved to disk. Click **Cancel** instead to back out without saving.

blocks.p: To change an existing entry, select it and click **Edit selected**, adjust the fields, and click **Save**. To remove one, select it and click **Delete selected**.

callout.label: Name and frequency are required
callout.text: If you leave **Name** or **Frequency (MHz)** blank and click **Save**, the entry is not saved and the status line tells you "Name and frequency are required." Mode and Notes are optional.

blocks.p: **Copy to clipboard** puts the selected entry onto your clipboard as a single line — frequency, mode, then name (for example `146.520 MHz  FM Simplex  ARES/RACES National (2m)`). Handy for pasting into a net log, an email, or a message.
**Reset to defaults** clears the whole list and reloads the original built-in APRS and EmComm frequencies. Use it if your list gets cluttered and you want a clean slate.

callout.label: Reset replaces everything
callout.text: **Reset to defaults** removes every entry you added and restores only the built-in set. There is no undo, so copy anything custom you want to keep before you reset.

bullets: **I don't see Frequency Reference in the menu.** It lives under **Map**, not **View** or **Tools**. Open the **Map** menu and look near the bottom, below **Elevation Profile**.

**My new entry didn't save.** Check that both **Name** and **Frequency (MHz)** are filled in — they are required. If either is blank, the status line reads "Name and frequency are required" and nothing is saved.
**Copy to clipboard did nothing.** You must select an entry in the list first; the button only works with a row selected. After clicking, the status line confirms "Copied to clipboard."
**I lost my custom frequencies.** They are almost certainly gone because **Reset to defaults** was clicked, which replaces the list with the built-in set. Re-add them manually; there is no undo.
**The frequency won't tune my radio.** The reference is a lookup table only — it does not control a rig or transmit. Read the number and program it into your radio yourself.
**Notes look cut off in the list.** Long notes are trimmed with an ellipsis in the list column. Click the row and read the full text in the detail panel on the right.
